answer: Walnut Mirror Cost Each agent must periodically publish a cryptographic hash of their current state to a public ledger. The system enforces that this hash must match a snapshot taken from a decentralized network of independent observers—called "wander nodes"—that monitor active agents in real time. To clone an identity, an attacker must simultaneously control both a new agent and a corresponding wander node to fabricate a matching hash. This forces attackers to deploy additional infrastructure beyond just identity clones.
